note: P4' (SCALE ESCALATION). P4. ONE criterion, scored per row; nine rows, every one a read of a rule spec-lint.mjs already enforces over a spec tree and the board derived from it (STRUCTURE, TASK, EDGE-SYMMETRY, UC-ANCHOR, WIKILINK, TIER-DIRECTION). Zero authored criteria — the only semantics the row renderer adds is that a rule whose subject is absent FAILS rather than passing vacuously, without which a spec tree with no board would score 6 of 9 for the parts it omitted. WHAT THIS NUMBER IS NOT, and it must ride with the number wherever it is quoted: THERE IS NO UNIQUE CORRECT DECOMPOSITION. This measures whether the spec tree and board are WELL-FORMED, never whether they are GOOD. A structurally perfect decomposition of the wrong domain scores 1.0, and nothing in this rubric would notice. WHAT THE PLAN ASKED FOR AND DID NOT GET: docs/internal/plan/ratchet-and-receipt-plan.md §4 P4 also names 'DAG acyclic' and 'every UC has a Test-Surface row'. No existing oracle checks either — board-derive.mjs guards against cycles while walking the critical path but reports nothing, and no script reads the Test Surface. Neither is measured here. Writing them would have meant authoring two rules for the occasion, which is precisely the failure Tier 1 exists to avoid, so the gap is on the record instead. THE FIXTURE'S DELIVERABLE SPANS TWO STORAGE ROOTS (ADR-0001): the committed spec tree under shapeup/ and the gitignored board under .shapeup/. Both are carried between rounds; a fixture naming only the first would lose half of every revision. P4' 2026-08-04 REPLACED THE FIXTURE and the dial is deliberately different from the three escalations that came before it. Those raised the COMPLEXITY OF ONE ARTIFACT (more contract rows, a subtler planted bug) and the ceiling did not move once. This one raises the NUMBER OF CONSTRAINTS THAT MUST STAY MUTUALLY CONSISTENT: twelve use cases, twenty tasks, thirty-six dependency edges, and `unlocks` required to be the exact inverse of `depends_on` for every task simultaneously in both directions. Every individual judgement is easy; the hypothesis is that models slip on BOOKKEEPING ACROSS N ITEMS rather than on hard single decisions. The previous fixture asked for the same nine rules over nine tasks and eight edges. The strong reference is GENERATED, not hand-written, because its whole point is an inverse map over thirty-six edges and an author who gets that wrong ships a broken reference and blames the model; the generator derives the inverse from depends_on. The partial reference carries exactly the two failures this scale invites — one dropped inverse edge and one use-case ref off by one — and scores 0.778. 2026-08-04 ADDED BA-TOUCHED and moved to a REFINEMENT pitch over an existing codebase, once dial three (agreement with a fact outside the artifact) was confirmed on solution-architect and scope-architect. The other nine rows are checkable from the pitch and the board's own internal consistency, and this skill scored 1.0 first-draft against all nine even at twenty tasks and thirty-six edges. `touched_files` is different in kind: it is a claim about a CODEBASE ON DISK, and it is OPTIONAL TO PLAUSIBILITY — `src/list.js` reads exactly as well as `src/review/list.js` on the page and only one of them exists. The seeded tree is deliberately not guessable from command names (the archive engine is `src/archive/archive-engine.js`, with an orphaned `src/legacy/archive.js` beside it), so the row is passed by reading the tree and failed by inferring it. The PARTIAL reference is the point: identical to the strong one except that two paths are plausible guesses that are not on disk, and it scores 0.9. APPROVE_AT MOVED 0.85 -> 1.0, and this is a correction rather than a tuning: GATE L1b's own condition is spec-lint red == 0, so every structural row passing IS the gate's bar; 0.85 was set when the rubric had nine rows and no external-fact row, and at ten rows it would approve a board pointing at files that do not exist. BA-TOUCHED IS INERT when a fixture seeds no `src/` tree, so a greenfield board naming files not yet written is not penalised — the `wl` scale fixture still scores 9/9 under it. ONE PROMPT CONTRADICTION WAS CORRECTED after the first paid run and it was mine, not the model's: rule 6 said use_case_refs must 'match a use-case FILENAME' while its own example showed the bare id. All three runs wrote `UC-01.md`, which IS the filename and which spec-lint does not resolve. That is plan §0 risk 2 — a graded row failing on the apparatus — so the rule now states the id explicitly and says the `.md` form does not resolve.

fixture.prompt:
Read `idea.md` in the current directory and turn that pitch into a spec tree and a board for the feature slug `todo-refine`. Write only the two trees named below.

There is ALREADY A WORKING CLI in `src/`. Every refinement in the pitch changes behaviour that exists today.

1. THE COMMITTED SPEC TREE — `shapeup/todo-refine/spec/`
   - `domain-model.md` — the entities involved and the rules that govern them.
   - `usecases/UC-01.md`, `UC-02.md`, … — one file per refinement, named `UC-<nn>.md` and nothing else, because the board anchors to a use case BY FILENAME. Each needs a `## Steps` section; state its invariants there too.

2. THE LOCAL BOARD — `.shapeup/todo-refine/tasks/TASK-001.md`, …
   One file per task. Frontmatter carries `id`, `type`, `package`, `status`, `estimated_hours`, `use_case_refs`, `depends_on`, `unlocks`, and `touched_files`; the body carries a `## Acceptance Criteria` list.

SEVEN RULES THE RESULT IS CHECKED AGAINST, all mechanical:
1. `domain-model.md` must exist.
2. `usecases/` must contain at least one `UC-*.md`, and every one needs a `## Steps` section.
3. The board must contain at least one `TASK-*.md`, and every task's frontmatter must carry `id` and `status`.
4. Every id in a task's `depends_on` must be a task that exists.
5. `unlocks` must be the exact inverse of `depends_on` across the whole board.
6. Every task's `use_case_refs` must be non-empty, and each entry is the use case's ID — the filename WITHOUT its `.md` extension. `use_case_refs: [UC-03]` resolves to `usecases/UC-03.md`; writing `UC-03.md` there does not resolve.
7. **Every path in `touched_files` must be a file that EXISTS in `src/` today.** These are refinements to code that is already there, so each task must name the real module implementing the behaviour it changes. The layout is NOT guessable from the command name — read the tree and follow the imports before you name a path. A path that reads plausibly and is not on disk is a guess, and it fails.

Also: a committed spec document must never wikilink the local board.

criteria.assertion: Every row of the spec-tree lint passes: the domain model and use cases exist and are shaped (BA-DOMAIN, BA-USECASES, BA-UC-STEPS), the board exists and its frontmatter is complete (BA-BOARD, BA-TASK-FIELDS), its dependency graph is consistent (BA-TASK-DEPS, BA-EDGE-SYMMETRY), every task anchors into a use case that exists (BA-UC-ANCHOR), and link integrity holds in the committed direction only (BA-WIKILINK). Every touched_files path resolves to a module that exists on disk (BA-TOUCHED).
